prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers. DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the e-reader through their website. The reader is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its e-book readers in a country where no e-book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an e-book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept.
prompt.question: How should DigiBooks launch and market the e-reader product in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What is an e-book reader exactly?
clarifying_info.a: An e-book reader is a software, hardware and network platform that utilizes wireless connectivity to enable users to shop for, download, browse, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, blogs, and other digital media.
DigiBooks uses an e-ink electronic paper display that features 16 shades of grey, allowing for a 12-hour battery life and easy readability.

clarifying_info.q: Has DigiBooks sold outside the US before?
clarifying_info.a: No, DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors in this new country?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table of three customer segments with their segment size (number of people) and the e-reader price point for each segment. Columns include: Segment, Size, and E-reader Price.

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two sales channels (Retail vs. Internet) across four metrics: Percent of Total Potential Market, E-book Gross Margin %, E-reader Gross Margin %, Penetration Rate, and Initial Investment.

framework: Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning: Identify which customer segment is ideal — Super Readers, Occasional Readers, or Rare Readers — based on revenue or profit potential
Product: Assess whether the existing product meets local needs or requires adaptation for this country
Price: Determine optimal price points for both the e-reader device and e-books; consider razor-and-blade pricing (low device price, margin on content)
Promotion: Identify effective marketing and promotional mechanisms to build awareness and trial in a market where only 1% have used an e-reader
Place / Distribution: Evaluate retail vs. internet sales channels for reaching customers and encouraging product trial
Selection of E-books: Ensure sufficient local-language and relevant book catalog is available to drive ongoing e-book purchases

questions.prompt: Prompt 1 — Using Exhibit 1 and a 3-year projection, which segment should DigiBooks target? (Note: the average price of an e-book is $10; e-books and e-reader have the same margin; calculate Revenue Potential ignoring probability of purchase and TVM)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential for each segment by combining e-reader revenue (one-time) and e-book revenue (annual books x price x 3 years), then multiply by segment size. The candidate who notices TVM or probability-of-purchase nuances earns bonus credit. Final answer: Occasional Readers with $8.5B.

math.setup: Revenue per person = (Books per year x $10/book x 3 years) + (E-reader price x 1). Multiply by segment size.
math.answer: Target Occasional Readers (OR) with the highest 3-year revenue potential of $8.5B

questions.prompt: Prompt 2 — DigiBooks is considering selling through retail stores vs. the internet. How would you evaluate this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should weigh pros and cons of each channel. Strong answers cover: Retail CONS — lower margin due to intermediaries, setup time and training costs; Retail PROS — encourages trial, joint marketing with retailers, retailer handles customer service and returns. Internet PROS — cheaper to establish, higher margins; Internet CONS — hard to encourage trial in a low-awareness market. Given only 1% usage and 50% awareness, trial encouragement is critical.

questions.prompt: Prompt 3 — DigiBooks has priced the e-reader at $100 and will target the Occasional Reader segment (20M people). Using Exhibit 2, calculate the 1-year gross profit for each sales channel after deducting initial investment. Which channel should DigiBooks choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate uses Exhibit 2 data plus the $10/book price and 20M OR segment size. Calculate gross profit = (e-book margin + e-reader margin) x penetrated customers, then subtract initial investment. Retail wins with $300M net profit vs. Internet's $100M.

math.setup: Gross Profit = [(Books/yr x book price x ebook GM%) + (ereader price x ereader GM%)] x (Segment size x Penetration) minus Initial Investment. Use 10 books/yr for OR segment, $10/book, $100 e-reader price, 20M segment size.
steps: Retail: [(10 x $10 x 50%) + ($100 x 30%)] x (20M x 40%) - $20M = [$50 + $30] x 8M - $20M = $80 x 8M - $20M = $640M - $20M... NOTE: Exhibit 2 shows each channel reaches 50% of total potential market first, so addressable = 20M x 50% = 10M. Revised: [$50 + $30] x (10M x 40%) - $20M = $80 x 4M - $20M = $320M - $20M = $300M
math.answer: Retail channel yields $300M net profit; Internet yields $100M. Choose Retail.

brainstorming.prompt: What advertising and go-to-market mechanisms could DigiBooks use to launch in this new country?

In-store demo stations to drive product trial

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch the e-reader targeting the Occasional Reader segment through the Retail sales channel
The Occasional Reader segment offers the highest 3-year revenue potential at $8.5B; the retail channel delivers $300M net 1-year profit on a $20M initial investment
risks: Low current usage (1%) means the market needs significant education and trial-driving investment
Retail channel requires time and money to establish; training and logistics costs add complexity
Dependence on a closed ecosystem (only DigiBooks e-books compatible) may limit adoption if content catalog is insufficient for local readers
No competitors today but market success may attract entrants over time
next_steps: Determine advertising and promotion strategy to build awareness and drive in-store trial
Assess whether existing product requires localization (language, content catalog, regulatory compliance)
Evaluate sourcing strategy: local manufacturing vs. importing from current facilities
Monitor competitive landscape and build contingency plans for potential market entrants
